heading_path: WS-POL-H — Public Accountability, Notice, Consent, and Feedback
sections.text: The committee generally agrees that transparency, communication, and accountability are essential to building trust in the use of AI in FCCPS. There is broad alignment that students and families should understand how AI is used and how it affects learning and student experience.

heading_path: WS-POL-H — Public Accountability, Notice, Consent, and Feedback
sections.text: The committee also recognizes that AI tools are already widely accessible outside of school environments and are increasingly part of students’ everyday reality. As a result, communication should not focus solely on restrictions or risk mitigation, but also on helping families understand how AI can be used responsibly to support learning.

heading_path: WS-POL-H — Public Accountability, Notice, Consent, and Feedback
sections.text: There are important tradeoffs regarding how these commitments are implemented. These include balancing clarity and transparency with administrative burden, ensuring consistency across classrooms while preserving educator flexibility, and determining when consent or opt-out mechanisms are appropriate versus impractical.

heading_path: WS-POL-H — Public Accountability, Notice, Consent, and Feedback
sections.text: The committee recommends that FCCPS adopt a clear, accessible, and practical approach to public accountability that builds trust and shared understanding across the community.

heading_path: WS-POL-H — Public Accountability, Notice, Consent, and Feedback
sections.text: The committee recommends that FCCPS provide clear, plain-language explanations of how AI is used in instructional and operational contexts. Communication should avoid technical jargon and be designed so that students and families can easily understand what AI is being used for, when it is being used, and what it means for their experience.

heading_path: WS-POL-H — Public Accountability, Notice, Consent, and Feedback
sections.text: Communication should be accessible across languages and community backgrounds. This includes providing translated materials and using multiple communication channels to ensure information reaches all families.

heading_path: WS-POL-H — Public Accountability, Notice, Consent, and Feedback
sections.text: Communication should also help families understand both the opportunities and the risks of AI use, so that expectations are not driven by uncertainty or fear, but by shared understanding.

heading_path: WS-POL-H — Public Accountability, Notice, Consent, and Feedback
sections.text: The committee recommends that families and students receive appropriate notice when AI tools are used in ways that meaningfully affect learning, evaluation, or student experience.

heading_path: WS-POL-H — Public Accountability, Notice, Consent, and Feedback
sections.text: Examples of such use may include:

heading_path: WS-POL-H — Public Accountability, Notice, Consent, and Feedback
sections.text: AI use in classroom instruction

heading_path: WS-POL-H — Public Accountability, Notice, Consent, and Feedback
sections.text: AI-supported feedback or assessment

heading_path: WS-POL-H — Public Accountability, Notice, Consent, and Feedback
sections.text: AI systems that process student data

heading_path: WS-POL-H — Public Accountability, Notice, Consent, and Feedback
sections.text: The level of notice should be proportional to the level of impact. Overly complex or universal notification requirements may reduce clarity and create unnecessary burden without improving understanding.

heading_path: WS-POL-H — Public Accountability, Notice, Consent, and Feedback
sections.text: The committee recognizes that in certain higher-risk contexts, including those involving sensitive data or meaningful impact on student experience, it may be appropriate to consider consent or opt-out mechanisms.

heading_path: WS-POL-H — Public Accountability, Notice, Consent, and Feedback
sections.text: At the same time, the committee emphasizes that overly rigid consent structures may be difficult to implement consistently and may unintentionally limit access to learning opportunities.

heading_path: WS-POL-H — Public Accountability, Notice, Consent, and Feedback
sections.text: Where opt-out options are provided, clear and equitable alternatives should be defined to ensure that students are not disadvantaged.

heading_path: WS-POL-H — Public Accountability, Notice, Consent, and Feedback
sections.text: The committee emphasizes that policy expectations must be clearly and consistently communicated to students and families.

heading_path: WS-POL-H — Public Accountability, Notice, Consent, and Feedback
sections.text: Students should receive clear guidance about when AI use is:

heading_path: WS-POL-H — Public Accountability, Notice, Consent, and Feedback
sections.text: permitted

heading_path: WS-POL-H — Public Accountability, Notice, Consent, and Feedback
sections.text: conditionally allowed

heading_path: WS-POL-H — Public Accountability, Notice, Consent, and Feedback
sections.text: or restricted

heading_path: WS-POL-H — Public Accountability, Notice, Consent, and Feedback
sections.text: Inconsistent expectations across classrooms may create confusion and undermine both learning and accountability. FCCPS should support alignment while allowing appropriate flexibility for educators.

heading_path: WS-POL-H — Public Accountability, Notice, Consent, and Feedback
sections.text: The committee also emphasizes the importance of engaging families as partners. Communication should support families in understanding how AI is being used to support learning, not only how it is being controlled.

heading_path: WS-POL-H — Public Accountability, Notice, Consent, and Feedback
sections.text: The committee recommends that FCCPS maintain a public-facing explanation of its approach to AI use. This may include:

heading_path: WS-POL-H — Public Accountability, Notice, Consent, and Feedback
sections.text: the types of AI tools in use

heading_path: WS-POL-H — Public Accountability, Notice, Consent, and Feedback
sections.text: the purposes they serve

heading_path: WS-POL-H — Public Accountability, Notice, Consent, and Feedback
sections.text: the safeguards in place

heading_path: WS-POL-H — Public Accountability, Notice, Consent, and Feedback
sections.text: Clear ownership should be established for oversight, including responsibility for:

heading_path: WS-POL-H — Public Accountability, Notice, Consent, and Feedback
sections.text: reviewing AI tools

heading_path: WS-POL-H — Public Accountability, Notice, Consent, and Feedback
sections.text: responding to concerns or incidents

heading_path: WS-POL-H — Public Accountability, Notice, Consent, and Feedback
sections.text: updating guidance as needed

heading_path: WS-POL-H — Public Accountability, Notice, Consent, and Feedback
sections.text: The committee recommends that FCCPS provide accessible channels for students, families, and staff to raise questions, concerns, or feedback related to AI use.

heading_path: WS-POL-H — Public Accountability, Notice, Consent, and Feedback
sections.text: This may include:

heading_path: WS-POL-H — Public Accountability, Notice, Consent, and Feedback
sections.text: a public feedback mechanism

heading_path: WS-POL-H — Public Accountability, Notice, Consent, and Feedback
sections.text: opportunities for community input

heading_path: WS-POL-H — Public Accountability, Notice, Consent, and Feedback
sections.text: structured ways to surface issues during implementation

heading_path: WS-POL-H — Public Accountability, Notice, Consent, and Feedback
sections.text: Feedback should be reviewed and used to inform ongoing improvements, not only collected.

heading_path: WS-POL-H — Public Accountability, Notice, Consent, and Feedback
sections.text: The committee recognizes that accountability requirements must be practical to implement. Overly complex communication, notice, or consent structures may create burden for staff and reduce effectiveness.

heading_path: WS-POL-H — Public Accountability, Notice, Consent, and Feedback
sections.text: Policy should define expectations at a high level, while allowing implementation details—such as communication formats, tools, and timelines—to be handled at the administrative level.
